metadata.title: Low-Level Design for User Story
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Create standalone low-level design (LLD) document for user stories that serves as foundational technical specification for subsequent SDLC phases including code development, test planning, and documentation.

steps.name: Get User Story Parameters
steps.output: User story details: title, description, acceptance criteria
steps.guidelineDescription: Teams use their preferred method to collect user story details from userStoryId: Jira, Azure DevOps, manual entry, requirements docs, etc.

steps.name: Understand User Story Context
steps.output: Context documentation with requirements, scope, success criteria

steps.name: Gather Relevant Information
steps.guidelineDescription: Teams use their preferred method to gather information: architecture docs, API specs, wiki pages, SME interviews, existing code patterns, etc.

steps.name: Analyze Current System
steps.output: System analysis report, affected components map, dependencies

feedbackLoop.description: If analysis reveals information gaps, return to Step 3 to gather additional data

steps.name: Create Low-Level Design Document
steps.guidelineDescription: Teams use their preferred LLD format: diagram types, sections, tools, level of detail, etc.

feedbackLoop.description: If design creation reveals information gaps, return to Step 3 to gather additional data

qAPattern.description: Each step handles its own Q&A as needed - no standalone Q&A step
qAPattern.workflow: When questions arise: identify open questions → present to user → wait for answers → continue with step

contents: Proposed design (architecture, data flow, class/sequence diagrams)
Technical specifications (API contracts, DB changes, config)
